summary: 1928 Plan 4AR fire lookout on a 10-foot enclosed timber tower in Plumas NF; staffed in fire season; 2017 rehabilitation; NHLR-registered 2019.

facts.design: rare, surviving California Region 5 Plan 4AR design on an enclosed 10-foot timber tower

staffing.as_of: undated NHLR page, read 2026-10-08; peakbagging photo page taken 2006

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Plumas National Forest

events.note: Register and 2017 report give 1928 as the build year; August 1928 newspaper says the station would be erected that fall
July 18, 1929 newspaper: Forest Service has just completed the lookout; lumber packed 1.5 miles up the mountain (July 4, 1929)
Myron Horn named as fire lookout for the 1931 season (June 5, 1931 item, forward-looking)
Lookout Horn sighted a fire that totally destroyed the old Burnham ranch house in Grizzly Valley; he alerted the Quincy dispatcher
June 13, 1936 item: Clyde Robinson to be lookout man during fire season
June 25, 1938 item: Victor Johnson moved to the lookout station for the fire season
Clay Bailey ill and hospitalized in Susanville; Maynard Pattan relief lookout (spelled Maynerd in the July 25, 1940 item)

On-site rehabilitation by Sustainable Group, Inc.: roof replaced with sheathing and fire-treated cedar shingles; catwalk, stairway and handrail repaired; access trail and peripheral stairs and walkways reconstructed
Registered October 24, 2019 as US 1337, CA 160; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: The Register describes the tower as an enclosed 10 foot timber tower; 10 feet is 3.05 m. The brief's 7.6 m equals about 25 feet and matches no source read here. Editor should check whether 7.6 m came from a different measure (for example the total height including cab).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives 8,070 ft (2,460 m), which matches the brief's 2459.7 m. The 2017 rehabilitation report and the Peakbagging photo page both give 8,327 ft, and an 1929 newspaper calls it 8,400 feet, the highest point in the Forest. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one.
The Register and the 2017 report give 1928. Newspapers show road building and station erection in 1928, with the lookout reported completed in July 1929. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief's height_m 7.6 conflicts with the Register's 10-foot tower; proposed 3.05 with correction. Elevation in the brief matches the Register; the 8,327 ft figure in the 2017 report and Peakbagging is a documented disagreement. The 1940 item spells the relief lookout's name Maynerd in one place and Maynard in another. Staffing is documented through 1940 only in newspapers; the Register's present-tense staffing claim is undated. Access and climbing status are not in the sources read.
